guide_line: Count protons, neutrons, and electrons for atoms and ions, then average the isotope masses.
steps: The atomic number Z is the proton count. It names the element and does not change when the atom becomes an ion. A neutral atom has the same number of electrons as protons.

The mass number A is protons plus neutrons. Neutrons = A − Z. Type an isotope as Cl-35: symbol, hyphen, mass number. Only the first letter of a symbol is capital, so Co is cobalt and CO is carbon monoxide.
Charge = protons − electrons. Losing electrons makes a positive ion, a cation. Gaining electrons makes a negative ion, an anion. Type the charge as 3+ or 2-.
Average atomic mass uses each isotope's fraction times its isotopic mass, not the whole-number mass number. Round the result to 4 significant figures. One electron has charge 1.602×10^−19 C.

worked_example.q: A neutral atom has 19 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its mass number?

similar_problem.q: A neutral atom has 17 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its mass number?
similar_problem.hint: This atom has 17 protons and 20 neutrons. Add those two counts.

problems.q: A neutral phosphorus atom has atomic number 15. How many protons does it have?
problems.why: The atomic number is the proton count. Phosphorus has 15 protons.
hints: Phosphorus has atomic number 15. That number is the proton count.

problems.q: Chlorine-37 has atomic number 17. How many neutrons are in one atom?
problems.why: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number. 37 − 17 = 20 neutrons.
hints: Chlorine-37 has mass number 37 and atomic number 17. Subtract 17 from 37.

problems.q: A sulfide ion has 16 protons and a charge of 2-. How many electrons does it have?
problems.why: Charge = protons − electrons. 16 − electrons = −2, so the ion has 18 electrons.
hints: This sulfide ion has charge 2- and 16 protons. Add 2 extra electrons to the proton count.

problems.q: An atom has 20 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its mass number?
hints: This atom has 20 protons and 20 neutrons. Add those two counts to get the mass number.

problems.q: An atom has 26 protons. Type the element symbol.
problems.why: Atomic number 26 is iron. The symbol is Fe.
hints: Atomic number 26 is iron. Type Fe with only the F capitalized.

problems.why: Sodium is atomic number 11. The symbol is Na.
hints: Sodium is atomic number 11. Type Na, not NA.

problems.q: Type the symbol for the element cobalt.
problems.why: Cobalt is one element, atomic number 27. The symbol is Co. CO would be carbon monoxide.
hints: Cobalt is one atom, atomic number 27. Type Co. Two capitals would mean carbon and oxygen.

problems.q: An ion has 13 protons and 10 electrons. What is its charge? Type it as 3+ or 2-.
problems.why: Charge = protons − electrons = 13 − 10 = 3+. The ion is positive because it has fewer electrons than protons.
hints: This ion has 13 protons and 10 electrons. Subtract the electrons from the protons and write the positive sign as 3+.

problems.q: A boron sample is 25.00% boron-10 (10.0129 amu) and 75.00% boron-11 (11.0093 amu). What is the average atomic mass? Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Take 0.2500 times 10.0129 amu and 0.7500 times 11.0093 amu. Add them, then round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: A neon sample is 90.00% neon-20 (19.9924 amu) and 10.00% neon-22 (21.9914 amu). What is the average atomic mass? Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Take 0.9000 times 19.9924 amu and 0.1000 times 21.9914 amu. Add them, then round to 4 significant figures.

problems.q: Neon-20 has mass 19.9924 amu and neon-22 has mass 21.9914 amu. A sample's average mass is 20.1923 amu. What percent of the atoms are neon-20? Use 4 significant figures.
hints: Solve 19.9924x + 21.9914(1 − x) = 20.1923 for x, then write the neon-20 percent with 4 significant figures.

problems.q: An Fe3+ ion has 26 protons. How many electrons does it have?
problems.why: A 3+ charge means 3 fewer electrons than protons. 26 − 3 = 23 electrons.
hints: Fe3+ still has 26 protons. It lost 3 electrons, so subtract 3 from 26.

problems.q: An atom has 35 protons and 44 neutrons. Type its isotope symbol as Br-79.
problems.why: 35 protons is bromine, symbol Br. Mass number = 35 + 44 = 79. The symbol is Br-79.
hints: 35 protons is bromine. Add 35 and 44 for the mass number, then type Br-79.

problems.q: One electron has charge 1.602×10^−19 C. An oil drop has charge −9.612×10^−19 C. How many extra electrons are on the drop?
problems.why: Divide the drop's charge by the electron charge. 9.612×10^−19 / 1.602×10^−19 = 6 extra electrons.
hints: Divide 9.612×10^−19 by 1.602×10^−19. The quotient is the extra-electron count on this drop.

problems.q: An atom loses electrons and the ion is positive. What is this kind of ion called?
problems.why: Losing electrons leaves more protons than electrons, so the ion is positive. A positive ion is a cation.
hints: This ion lost electrons, so protons outnumber electrons. Name the positive ion.

problems.q: An atom gains electrons and the ion is negative. What is this kind of ion called?
problems.why: Gaining electrons makes the charge negative. A negative ion is an anion.
hints: This ion gained electrons, so the charge is negative. Name the negative ion.

problems.q: An ion has 8 protons and 10 electrons. Type the symbol with the charge, as in Na+ or Cl-.
problems.why: 8 protons is oxygen. Charge = 8 − 10 = 2−. The symbol is O2-.
hints: 8 protons is oxygen. Two extra electrons make the charge 2-. Type O2-, not O2+.

problems.q: Calcium has atomic number 20. One calcium atom loses 2 electrons. How many protons are in the ion?
problems.why: Losing electrons changes the charge, not the atomic number. The ion still has 20 protons.
hints: Electrons left the atom. The atomic number does not change, so the proton count stays 20.

problems.q: A neon sample is 70.00% neon-20 (19.9924 amu), 1.000% neon-21 (20.9938 amu), and 29.00% neon-22 (21.9914 amu). What is the average atomic mass? Round to 4 significant figures.
hints: Turn 70.00%, 1.000%, and 29.00% into decimals. Multiply each by its isotopic mass, not by 20, 21, or 22, then add and round to 4 significant figures.
